_comment: epochLength 600 — widens the `PotentialPParamsUpdate` phase so the futurePParams
parity sampler can reach its non-vacuous condition instead of relying on luck.
MECHANISM. `FuturePParams` has three constructors, and `solidifyFuturePParams` maps
`PotentialPParamsUpdate Nothing -> NoPParamsUpdate` and
`PotentialPParamsUpdate (Just pp) -> DefinitePParamsUpdate pp` at the point of no
return, 2*stabilityWindow = 2*(3k/f) into the epoch. So `PotentialPParamsUpdate` is an
EPOCH PHASE: it holds from the boundary until that point, carrying `Nothing` when no
pparam-changing action is pending in the frozen pulser and `Just pp` when one is.
With the repo default epochLength=400, k=40, f=0.5:
2 * stabilityWindow = 480  >  400
so the solidify point precedes the epoch's own first slot and the phase survives only
from the boundary tick until the next one — three or four slots out of four hundred.
v2.6.0's gate saw 6 window samples in 548 comparisons (~1%), which is exactly this.
A 900s Round 2 measured 514 comparisons, 0 diffs, potential_samples=0 across 2
boundaries, and the sampler correctly reported INCONCLUSIVE — two implementations
agreeing that nothing is pending is not evidence (#977, and the #992
hardcoded-empty-pulser lesson).
At epochLength=600 the solidify point (480) falls INSIDE the epoch, so the phase is
~480 slots out of 600 rather than ~3. Reaching non-vacuity stops being a coin flip.
A WRONG DIAGNOSIS WAS TRIED FIRST AND IS RECORDED SO IT IS NOT REPEATED. On seeing
`NoPParamsUpdate` at slot 43 of epoch 0 I concluded the phase does not exist without a
ratified ParameterChange, deleted this overlay, and lengthened the round instead. That
measurement discriminates NOTHING: at epochLength=400 the solidify point is already
behind us at slot 43, so `NoPParamsUpdate` is precisely what the phase model predicts.
Payload-absent is not constructor-absent.
The three devnet invariants still hold, and they are why 600 and not less:
3k/f = 240 <= 600   chain stability
4k/f = 320 <= 600   the RUPD pulser fits inside an epoch
6k/f = 480 <  600   the solidify point falls inside the epoch  <- the whole point
Cost: epochs are 600s, so the RUPD boundary 1->2 lands at slot 1200 (~20 min) instead
of 800. A round using this overlay must run long enough to reach it — 1800s — or the
byte-exact pot-parity check has nothing to compare.
Rounds that need this must name it via LD_SHELLEY_SPEC_EXTRA and must ALSO export
LD_EPOCH_LENGTH=600: the parity samplers derive the epoch as slot / ${LD_EPOCH_LENGTH:-400},
so leaving it unset would miscount every boundary.
